Are Property Taxes Eating Into Your Rental Profits?

For a rental-property owner, every expense matters.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

THE SHORT ANSWER

A well-supported residential appraisal can provide an independent perspective on a rental property’s market value, particularly when the assessor’s estimate seems inconsistent with comparable sales or the property’s condition. Reddy Appraisal LLC works with Southern Arizona investors who want reliable valuation information before making decisions about holding, refinancing, selling, or evaluating a possible tax assessment appeal.

Include property tax in the investment picture

For a rental-property owner, every expense matters. Insurance, maintenance, vacancies, and financing already compete for your monthly cash flow, and property taxes can further reduce your return. If you own a duplex, triplex, fourplex, or single-family rental in Tucson, reviewing your property valuation is one more part of protecting your investment.

Review the assessment carefully

Begin by checking the assessor’s property description, classification, full cash value, and limited property value. Then evaluate whether the valuation reasonably reflects the property’s actual characteristics and relevant market evidence. Rental income and operating expenses can be informative, but they need to be interpreted carefully: an investor’s cash flow is not automatically the same as taxable property value, and Arizona’s valuation and appeal rules determine which evidence is appropriate.
